articleTitle: Harmonic management for large, multimotor DC drive systems
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Three Phase LV Industrial Supplies: Harmonic Pollution and Recent Developments in Remedies
abstract: Despite recent advances in power switching technologies phase controlled rectification remains a most useful method of controlling variable speed motors. Unfortunately, such power converters are a powerful source of harmonic currents with a characteristic pattern. The author argues that with increasing installed capacities and growing concern for power supply quality it is essential to manage these harmonics to avoid unwanted interference with other equipment on the supply network.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Harmonic currents produced by variable speed drives with uncontrolled rectifier inputs
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Three Phase LV Industrial Supplies: Harmonic Pollution and Recent Developments in Remedies
abstract: The authors describe the harmonic currents produced in a power supply system by variable speed drives with uncontrolled rectifier inputs, mainly six-pulse. The analysis was undertaken by computer simulation using a commercially available simulator. The harmonic currents are defined and controlled principally by the nonlinearity of the rectifiers together with the inductances within the drive and the power supply system. The effect of inductance, and other factors, on the harmonic currents is discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Harmonic suppression filter for offshore interconnected power system
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Three Phase LV Industrial Supplies: Harmonic Pollution and Recent Developments in Remedies
abstract: In theUK offshore industry there has been an increase, over recent years, in the number of satellite platforms that are fed from mother platforms by submarine power cables of significant length. On such systems electrical resonances caused by the combination of submarine cable capacitance and mother platform power transformer and generator inductance can occur. When combined with harmonic currents produced by power converters on the system, excessive voltage distortion levels can be generated. The authors described the analysis of harmonic distortion on Total Oil Marine's North Alwyn performance together with the new Dunbar platform. The Dunbar platform is fed by two 22.5 km submarine cables from the North Alwyn platform.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Long term monitoring of power systems harmonics
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Three Phase LV Industrial Supplies: Harmonic Pollution and Recent Developments in Remedies
abstract: The author describe the results of a test programme which set out to discover properties of power system background harmonic distortion by means of long term measurements. Measurements were carried out at a number of locations within the UK and offshore, over periods of up to two weeks in order that the full record of variation be obtained over week days and week ends. The results have been used to determine a suitable model for background distortion.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Harmonic reduction by transformer phase displacement
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Three Phase LV Industrial Supplies: Harmonic Pollution and Recent Developments in Remedies
abstract: Among the many techniques for remedying harmonic pollution, one possibility seems to have escaped consideration. Here, the author describes a practical investigation and results of the effect, at the point of common coupling, of introducing phase displacement between two separate, highly distorted loads. The background to the work is the effect on a small, three phase distribution system when switch mode power supplies form a significant proportion of the load.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Harmonic distortion and voltage spike calculations
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Three Phase LV Industrial Supplies: Harmonic Pollution and Recent Developments in Remedies
abstract: Harmonic currents and voltages calculations in power system have traditionally been carried out either using 'hand' calculations or using computer program which have been developed from fundamental frequency load flow program. The common features of these two methods is that they are both frequency domain calculations and also rely heavily on assumed data from manufacturers about the harmonics generated by their products. In the case of electric drives this information is often in the form of a look-up table. Here, the author discusses the limitation of such methods. He suggests that for many systems a time domain approach to harmonic distortion calculations is needed and that a fuller representation is often needed especially for low voltage system where the concept of an infinite busbar or a fixed harmonic load are no longer valid. The approach described is based on experience gained on offshore oil platform electrical system and ship electrical systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: IEC/CENELEC STANDARD and reports relevant to the harmonic emissions of LC industrial equipment
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Three Phase LV Industrial Supplies: Harmonic Pollution and Recent Developments in Remedies
abstract: With full implementation of the EMC Directive due at the end of 1995 there is considerable pressure on IEC and CENELEC technical committees to publish generic, basic and product standards relevant to all electromagnetic phenomena. In the case of harmonics it has been CIGRE Working Group 36-05 which has had the greatest impact on standards work. Whilst it has been relatively easy to establish LV and MV compatibility levels for harmonic distortion in public supply networks it has been difficult to obtain international agreement on the- establishment of the relationship between them and the emission limits of particular equipment. The standards and reports described by the author either influence or directly relate to the harmonic emissions of three phase industrial equipment.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Sinusoidal rectification for harmonic elimination-technology explained
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Three Phase LV Industrial Supplies: Harmonic Pollution and Recent Developments in Remedies
abstract: The need for power systems to reduce the levels of network harmonic pollution is quite clear. Activity within the European Legislative bodies and other international organisations is causing an increasing awareness of the problems associated with power supply waveform distortion. One of the causes of this waveform distortion is conventional 6-pulse rectifying equipment found in the input stages of many types of electrical equipment. The author outlines an alternative technique for power conversion that draws a continuous sinusoidal current from the power network under all load conditions. The performance of production sinusoidal rectifying equipment is illustrated with waveforms derived from product type testing.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
